title: Subjects’ beliefs about experience, not experiences, are the primary data

statements.text: The primary interpreted data are subjects’ beliefs about their experiences. If experiences outrun beliefs, the extra experiences are as inaccessible to the subject as to observers. If beliefs outrun experiences, the beliefs are what needs explaining. Treating beliefs as the maximal data avoids commitment to spurious data.

sources.quote: then it is your beliefs that we need to explain, not the non-existent experiences
is the way to avoid any commitment to spurious data
